The dynamic preference field must be exactly muted or archived and its value boolean; current native roster authorization precedes fixed-column SQL bound to c.owner. Prototype/arbitrary fields cannot reach the assignment.

Canonical event quality is recomputed from known event types and frozen numeric weights before scoring. Only known scoreable product/seller events reach incrementSignal; prototype names cannot pass the known-event gate.
Cookie keys accumulate string values into Object.create(null), preventing inherited prototype setters. Authentication still resolves a current stored session; cookie parsing is not authorization.
The malformed-encoding fallback writes strings into the same null-prototype dictionary; no inherited setters or executable values are introduced.

Actual related action is authorizeConversationActivity at line 95. Common service credential, bounded command validation and live ticket/session authorization precede execute. The activity authorizer always checks current native proof, binding, membership, mutual consent and block policy; selecting another command does not expose activity.

history-tasks selects dispatch, not permission. SQL binds owner, donor/recipient actor, expiry and active epoch; each row then checks its actual conversation membership/freeze/roster before disclosure.
Stored history transfer use must match the authorized conversation, owner, same epoch, expiry and active endpoints. The previously fixed cross-conversation defect remains covered by negative tests.

room-reserve dispatch retains signed actor/owner authorization; changes require stored admin role/current membership and initial creation validates active device/key-package ownership. Room acceptance cannot be reached without its distinct transition and signature checks.

Preference dispatch follows current native room membership. Saves restrict field/value, bind owner and fixed SQL columns, and reject stale revisions/changed retries. Returning preferences is not acceptance of a transition.

room-accept dispatch follows current membership and active transition lookup; IDs/transfer hash must match canonical state and the actor must occur in the proposed roster before signature verification.

Signature is verified against exact group, epoch, stored transfer hash, authenticated owner and actor using the pinned roster MLS key. Malformed or substituted acceptances are rejected before insertion.

Each invite operation has explicit authority: create/list/revoke/decline require current native membership/admin policy; requests require live scoped token, privacy/block/expiry checks. A request/confirm never inserts native membership or bypasses MLS admission.
Invite request listing requires current room authority/admin role; SQL further excludes blocked recipients and expired/revoked records.
Revoke requires current native admin authority and matches invite content type/room ID; the supplied ID alone grants no revocation permission.
Decline requires current native room/admin authority and validates recipient scope before a room-level request update.
Confirm requires an existing live token-bound request and canonical room membership; no membership is created by the confirmation branch.
The JSON-type condition only rejects unsupported input. Service credential checks precede it; bounded parsing and live ticket/session authorization remain mandatory after it.
Login input format is checked before account/password verification and throttling. Valid-looking input still cannot issue a session without the verified password/current account policy.
Admin input format validation precedes mandatory password verification, staff role and throttling; choosing valid input cannot skip privileged authentication.
Step-up resolves the current authenticated marketplace/staff user first and verifies the actual password before replacing/elevating session state.
Logout only selects the admin-login presentation after local auth state is cleared. It issues no staff credential or backend permission.

Product upload resolves an authenticated seller first, validates payload and requires uploadedBy equality with that seller; repost source ownership is checked separately. The client field cannot replace canonical owner identity.
The route chooses a UI screen; isStaffUser and backend authorization remain independent. A chosen URL does not issue privileged sessions or allow admin endpoints.
Boot shows an admin login screen; it creates no privileged session and changes no backend role/access rules.
